# Tŷ Mawr — The Great House Farm Story — llms.txt

> The true story of the Williams/Buckler family and Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, Wales, in 129 scenes across 8 acts with a prologue and epilogue, in strict date order.
> Every scene is drawn from the Great House Farm Wiki evidence catalogue (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/) and carries its evidence links.
> Structured JSON (acts, cast, scenes, evidence, stable ids): https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/api/timeline.json
> Printable script (static HTML, no JavaScript needed): https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/story/
> Storyboard: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?view=storyboard · Cast: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?view=cast · Any scene: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?event=<id>

## About

The Williams family lived at Great House Farm, beside St Dochdwy's Church, Llandough, for generations (by the family's account since 1667). The family's case is that the farm was two parcels: the house parcel (Parcel A), which passed out of the Bute estate to Daniel Thomas in 1877 and became the family's freehold when quarrying ended in 1928, and the eastern fields (Parcel B), which went to Western Ground Rents in 1938 and to BP. The possession cases of 1955, 1962, 1974 and BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 decided possession; none of them examined the documents that bear on the family's title to the house parcel. BP demolished the farmhouse on 6 December 1988, the morning after Cadw declined to list it, before it could be fully recorded. In 1994 an early-medieval cemetery of 1,026 burials was excavated on the site. Since 2025 the family have been recovering the missing records, and Cadw, Heneb and HM Land Registry's Independent Complaints Reviewer are now investigating. The family's case is that fraud and concealment kept the title documents from the courts, so the case can be reopened.

Truth labels follow the Wiki: documented fact, family evidence, reconstruction, legal inference and unresolved. The 1978–79 Llandough Roman Villa is a separate site south of the church.

## Full Timeline

129 scenes, in strict date order.

### P.1 (1). c. AD 650 — The church beside the farm

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-06500101-1 · Date: 0650-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

Beside the farm stands St Dochdwy's church, thought to stand on the site of an early Christian monastery. The published reference for this is still being traced.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### P.2 (2). 12th – 14th century — Medieval occupation

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-12000101-1 · Date: 1200-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Archaeological record

People are living on the site in the Middle Ages: pottery of the 12th to early 14th centuries is later found on the slope just north-east of the house. The Royal Commission classes the house, Tŷ Mawr ('Great House'), as sub-medieval and probably 17th-century, possibly with a medieval core like Brynwell in neighbouring Leckwith.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### P.3 (3). 1552 – 1829 — Cydfin, or Tŷ Mawr

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-15520101-1 · Date: 1552-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Estate papers

The Llandough manorial leases later kept in the Bute estate papers run from 1552 to 1829. The catalogue lists leases of 'Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm (107 a.)' — the farm's older name.

- Estate papers: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records D 219: Llandough manorial leases and agreements, 1552–1829 — https://archives.library.wales/index.php/llandough-manorial-leases-and-agreements
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### P.4 (4). Mid 16th – late 18th century — The Vaughans of Great House

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-15600101-1 · Date: 1560-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Heritage record

Great House is the chief freehold farm of the parish. The Vaughans, a minor gentry family, hold it from the mid-16th century until the late 18th; their memorials survive in Llandough church and churchyard.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### P.5 (5). 1667 — The Williamses arrive

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-16670101-1 · Date: 1667-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

By Mary Williams's account, her family's life at Great House begins in 1667. Family tradition remembers it as a purchase; later estate records treat the family as tenants. No earlier written source has yet been found.

> The family's case: The family hold, from Mary's statement and the 1974 Daily Telegraph report, that their ancestors acquired Tŷ Mawr in about 1667.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — origins — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/#origins

### P.6 (6). Early 19th century — The Bute Estate takes the freehold

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-18000101-1 · Date: 1800-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Heritage record

Early in the 19th century the Bute Estate acquires the freehold of Great House. The manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith are held in the house, and the estate modernises it, as it does neighbouring Brynwell.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Wiki page: The Bute Estate — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bute-estate/

### P.7 (7). 1818 – 1821 — Llandough enters Bute's books

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-18180101-2 · Date: 1818-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Estate papers

From 1818 the chief rents of Llandough are taken into the Bute manorial rental, and from 1821 Llandough and Cogan appear in the Bute estate rentals.

- Estate papers: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records R1: Glamorgan Estate rentals — https://archives.library.wales/index.php/glamorgan-estate-rentals

### P.8 (8). 1824 — Stewart's survey

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-18240101-1 · Date: 1824-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Estate papers

David Stewart surveys and values the Bute Glamorgan estate. The wiki's research records the farm under the name 'Cedfin'; the exact wording in the survey is still to be checked.

- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations (Stewart survey, D/d B E/1–2) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### P.9 (9). c. 1840 — From "Great House" to "farm"

Prologue: An Ancient Place · Scene id: ghf-18400101-1 · Date: 1840-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Public record

Census and tithe records start describing the place in different ways — 'Great House', then 'Great House Farm'. The records alone do not show the change was deliberate.

> The family's case: The family's case is that re-describing the manorial court house as a mere farmhouse wore away its standing, and theirs, and hid what the building was.

- Wiki page: Farmhouse Nomenclature — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/farmhouse-nomenclature/
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### I.1 (10). c. 1858 — Bones by the church

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18580101-1 · Date: 1858-01-01 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Museum record

Workmen digging foundations at Llandough Church Farm find about six skeletons with a medieval iron spearhead and a rowel spur. The bones are reburied by the church stile. A 1931 letter records the finds for the National Museum, which takes in the spur and spearhead in 1963 (accession 63.24).

- Museum record: 1931 letter, Museum Wales file 63.24 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/ghf-e106-r33-a1-1931-letter-museum-wales-file-63-24/
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### I.2 (11). c. 1870 — The soldier under the floor

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18700101-1 · Date: 1870-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Family tradition tells of a soldier in armour, with horse, lance and small shield, found beneath the dining-room floor. The Daily Telegraph repeats the story in 1974, and in 1988 the Royal Commission notes a report of 'armour' under the rear wing. No primary record of the find has been located, and the 1988 note dates it to c. 1880. Museum Wales says the medieval ironwork it holds came from Church Farm in 1858, not Great House.

> The family's case: The family see the find as proof of the site's antiquity — a lead nobody followed up before the house was destroyed.

- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974 (dates the find to "about 1870") — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### I.3 (12). 1876 – c. 1912 — The limeworks

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18760101-1 · Date: 1876-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Estate papers

The Bute Estate lets about 33 acres that had been part of Great House Farm for the Llandough Limeworks, which work the stone until about 1912.

> The family's case: The family's case, from Mary's statement, is that the farm was given up for quarrying on terms that the freehold of the house parcel would pass to her grandfather once quarrying ended. That agreement is among the missing papers.

- Wiki page: Llandough Limeworks — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/llandough-limeworks/

### I.4 (13). 1877 — The farm is split in two

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18770101-1 · Date: 1877-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Mary's statement

The Bute Estate serves notice to quit, then sells the farmhouse and about 10 acres to the quarryman Daniel Thomas, keeping about 9 acres of fields. The Williamses become tenants of both. From here the farm is two parcels: the house (Parcel A) and the eastern fields (Parcel B). The deed is missing.

> The family's case: The family contend that the 1877 sale took the house parcel out of the Bute title for good, so it could never pass to WGR or BP.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — the sale — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#sale-1877
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — plan — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#plan
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/

### I.5 (14). 6 November 1877 — The Bute lease

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18771106-1 · Date: 1877-11-06 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Estate papers

The Bute Estate grants John Williams a lease, held today at Glamorgan Archives. On the family's reconstruction it covers the fields, Parcel B. A copy is still to be obtained.

- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — Bute lease — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#sale-1877

### I.6 (15). 11 November 1891 — Three geese

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18911111-1 · Date: 1891-11-11 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Newspaper

Three geese are stolen from "Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough". The court report is contemporary proof that John Williams is living at the farm.

- Newspaper: 1891 court report — farmyard theft — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n01

### I.7 (16). May 1897 — Marconi

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18970501-1 · Date: 1897-05-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

Marconi's wireless trials at Lavernock Point send the first signals across open sea, to Flat Holm. Family tradition holds that Thomas Williams of Great House carted Marconi and his equipment to the point. The trials are documented; the family's part is not yet proved.

- Newspaper: Press report of the Lavernock trials, 1897 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n02

### I.8 (17). 23 February 1905 — A Bute conveyance

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-19050223-1 · Date: 1905-02-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

A Bute conveyance of this date later turns up on the WA231076 registration file and is noted on the woodland title WA735527. On the current reading it concerns Parcel A; what it conveyed is still to be confirmed.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### I.9 (18). 1908 — John Williams takes over

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-19080101-1 · Date: 1908-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Mary's statement

Mary's grandfather dies. Her father, John Williams, takes over both tenancies: the house from the Thomas side, the fields from Bute.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: John Williams — 1908 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/john-williams/#y1908

### I.10 (19). 1910 or 1911 — Frederick Buckler is born

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-19100101-1 · Date: 1910-01-01 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Family account

Frederick Buckler is born. The year is worked back from his death in 1967, aged 56; his certificates are awaited.

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/

### I.11 (20). 10 August 1913 — Mary is born

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-19130810-1 · Date: 1913-08-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

Mary Williams is born in the farmhouse, the daughter of John Williams. She will live there for the rest of her life.

- Wiki page: Mary Williams — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/
- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/

### II.1 (21). February 1916 — "The whole farm"

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19160201-1 · Date: 1916-02-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

Bute lets "the whole farm" to John Williams on a yearly tenancy. The tenancy is known only from the 1987 judgment and the 1989 Commission decision; the document itself has not been found.

> The family's case: The family's case is that "whole farm" is a later description, and that without the original plan it cannot show the house parcel was ever in this tenancy.

- Court record: The 1916 Tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1916-tenancy/#grant
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Farm / Whole Farm Nomenclature — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/whole-farm-nomenclature/

### II.2 (22). 15 May 1924 — An agreement on file

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19240515-1 · Date: 1924-05-15 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Land Registry record

An agreement of this date sits on the WA231076 registration file. Its contents and effect are unknown, and which parcel it concerns is not yet clear.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### II.3 (23). 1928 — The last rent

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19280101-1 · Date: 1928-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

The last quarry machinery leaves. John Williams pays a final rent of about £4 to Alfred Thomas, and from then on, Mary recalls, he regards the farm as his own. She saw the receipt; it is now missing.

> The family's case: The family's case is that the 1877 bargain took effect in 1928, making John Williams freeholder of the house parcel.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — takes effect 1928 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#takes-effect

### II.4 (24). 1936 — Mary marries Frederick

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19360101-1 · Date: 1936-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Mary marries Frederick Buckler, who comes to live with her at the farmhouse. They will have seven children.

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — marriage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#marriage

### II.5 (25). c. 1937 – 40 — The eldest son

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19370101-1 · Date: 1937-01-01 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Family account

Frederick and Mary's eldest son is born. The date rests on family belief; his birth entry has still to be traced.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### II.6 (26). 1938 — Sold to Western Ground Rents

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19380101-1 · Date: 1938-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

Bute conveys its reversion on the 1916 tenancy to Western Ground Rents Ltd.

> The family's case: If the house parcel left Bute's hands in 1877, it cannot have been part of this sale. The family expect the 1938 conveyance, when it is produced, to show only the eastern fields being sold.

- Wiki page: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#y1938
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### II.7 (27). May 1939 — The revised tenancy

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19390501-1 · Date: 1939-05-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Document

WGR grants John Williams a revised tenancy. Its plan shows the fields east of the house.

> The family's case: The family have seen the 1939 tenancy: it covers the eastern fields only. The house parcel is not in it.

- Wiki page: 1938–39: the 1939 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#y1939
- Wiki page: The 1939 tenancy plan — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#plan

### II.8 (28). c. 1940 — Twelve years

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19400101-1 · Date: 1940-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

Twelve years on from 1928, John Williams is still in the house. On Mary's account, no rent has been paid on it since.

> The family's case: The family's case is that twelve years' rent-free occupation of the house parcel from 1928 gave John Williams title by about 1940, if he did not already own it under the 1877 bargain.

- Wiki page: 1938–39 — c. 1940 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#c1940

### II.9 (29). 1944 — Frederick runs the farm

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19440101-1 · Date: 1944-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Mary's statement

The War Agricultural Executive Committee is unhappy with the farm, and Frederick Buckler takes over running it as manager for John Williams.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: John Williams — 1944 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/john-williams/#y1944

### II.10 (30). c. 1948 – 49 — Billy is born

Act II: Two Parcels · Scene id: ghf-19480101-1 · Date: 1948-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

William (Billy) Buckler is born at the farm. He will live there until the eviction of 1988.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/#william

### III.1 (31). 2 February 1949 — An unwritten tenancy

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19490202-1 · Date: 1949-02-02 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

John Williams surrenders his tenancy, and his son-in-law Frederick Buckler's yearly tenancy from WGR begins. It is never put in writing. Mary is not named in it.

> The family's case: The family's case is that this unwritten tenancy of the fields was later treated as a tenancy of "the farm", blurring the line between the two parcels.

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — the 1949 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/

### III.2 (32). June 1950 – c. 1952 — The blanket box

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19500601-1 · Date: 1950-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

A Penarth estate agent puts a lodger in the farmhouse. He stays about two years, and later tells Mary he took 'the papers which were in the blanket box including the agreement relating to the farm' and handed them to the agent.

> The family's case: The family contend that the documents proving their title were taken from their home just before the first possession proceedings — and that the missing title papers recorded around 1951 are those same papers.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — papers taken — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#papers-taken

### III.3 (33). 10 October 1952 — The letting is dropped

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19521010-1 · Date: 1952-10-10 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

WGR's agents write that they will not go ahead with the letting to Frederick.

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — 1952 letter — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949

### III.4 (34). 1953 — The last rent on the fields

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19530101-1 · Date: 1953-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

Frederick makes his last rent payment. The family say they paid nothing further to anyone.

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### III.5 (35). 2 February 1955 — The first possession order

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19550202-1 · Date: 1955-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

The High Court makes a possession order against Frederick Buckler alone, worded for the whole farm. Mary is not a party. On 4 July 1955 the landlord takes everything except the farmhouse and garden — Mary has just come out of hospital and objects strongly — and the family stay on in the house.

> The family's case: The family contend the order was about the fields Frederick rented, worded as if the two parcels were one. Mary, who claimed the house, was never heard.

- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#order
- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — enforcement — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#enforcement

### III.6 (36). 1959 — Mary says no

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19590101-1 · Date: 1959-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

WGR offers Mary a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden. She refuses: the house is hers. She tells them documents prove it — but the papers from the blanket box are gone.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — 1959 refusal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#refusal-1959
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### III.7 (37). 29 March 1961 — A deed on file

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19610329-1 · Date: 1961-03-29 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Land Registry record

A deed of this date sits on the WA231076 registration file. Its contents are unknown, and which parcel it concerns is not yet clear.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### III.8 (38). 11 December 1962 — The second possession order

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19621211-1 · Date: 1962-12-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

Judge Temple Morris QC orders possession of the farmhouse and garden, with mesne profits back to 1955, against Frederick and Mary on WGR's claim. The order is not enforced.

> The family's case: The family question whether a county court could hear the case at all: its limit in 1962 was a rateable value of £100.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#order

### III.9 (39). 1963 — Three skeletons

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19630101-1 · Date: 1963-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

Three skeletons are reported in a utility trench near the church. The account comes from a secondary research file; the 1963 record itself is still being traced.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### III.10 (40). June 1963 — Committal

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19630601-1 · Date: 1963-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The mesne profits under the 1962 order are partly enforced against Frederick, and committal proceedings follow.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — committal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#committal

### III.11 (41). January – March 1965 — Another tenancy refused

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19650301-1 · Date: 1965-03-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Document

WGR will not let Frederick the fields. On 2 March its agents offer 'Mrs Williams' a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2 a week. It is not signed or returned, and no rent is paid.

> The family's case: The family see it as another attempt to turn what Mary claimed as her own into a tenancy she never accepted.

- Wiki page: The 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#offer-1965
- Wiki page: Mary Williams — 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#offer-1965

### III.12 (42). 1964 – 67 (date uncertain) — A rumoured sale

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19640101-1 · Date: 1965-06-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

A cousin's account says the eldest son sold "our land parcel" through a solicitor, without his parents knowing. What was sold, if anything, is unknown; no document has been found.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — rumoured sale — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/#rumoured-sale

### III.13 (43). 1967 — Frederick dies

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19670101-1 · Date: 1967-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Frederick Buckler dies, aged 56. Mary takes back her maiden name, Williams, and stays on in the farmhouse. An estate paper gives December 1965; the family take 1967.

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#death

### III.14 (44). 1968 – 69 — The eldest son leaves

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19680901-1 · Date: 1968-09-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

The eldest son's household leaves the farm.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/#rumoured-sale

### IV.1 (45). 31 December 1969 — BP buys in

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19691231-1 · Date: 1969-12-31 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

WGR sells to BP Pension Trust Ltd. This conveyance is later recited as the root of BP's title — yet it is missing from the Land Registry files.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.2 (46). 16 June 1970 — The village green

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19700616-1 · Date: 1970-06-16 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Public record

Land by Leckwith Road is registered as village green VG41. The current reconstruction places it in Parcel A; the boundary is still to be confirmed.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### IV.3 (47). 25 July 1972 — Permission for houses

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19720725-1 · Date: 1972-07-25 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Planning permission for housing on the site is granted — while Mary is still living in the farmhouse.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### IV.4 (48). 1974 — A survey in difficult circumstances

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19740101-1 · Date: 1974-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

H.J. Thomas surveys the ground floor for the Royal Commission. The first floor and roof cannot be examined: the house 'remained partially recorded because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute'.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### IV.5 (49). 15 April 1974 — Open day

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19740415-1 · Date: 1974-04-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Mary, now 60, opens her home to the public 'to show what the nation is losing'. Hundreds come and about a thousand sign a petition. The Daily Telegraph reports that permission for about 13 houses has gone to the BP pension trust, that Mary will refuse to move, that ownership has been disputed for some 25 years, and that her solicitors say she has a valid claim.

> The family's case: Mary was claiming ownership in public, with legal backing, more than ten years before the case that took her home.

- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, 'Open day to save ancient Welsh house' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Wiki page: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action

### IV.6 (50). 3 July 1974 — Mary pleads ownership

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19740703-1 · Date: 1974-07-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

BP Pension Trust brings a new possession action. Mary pleads that she owns the house, and the Limitation Act 1939. The case is part-heard and never relisted.

> The family's case: The family contend BP let the title fight lapse, withdrew the warrant and sent a licence instead — and that her claim was never extinguished.

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the action — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### IV.7 (51). 19 September 1974 — Leave to enforce

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19740919-1 · Date: 1974-09-19 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The county court (Judge Watkin Powell, per the family archive) gives BP leave to enforce the 1962 order, with no warrant before 31 October. Mary was given no notice; her solicitors appeal.

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the warrant — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#warrant

### IV.8 (52). 31 October 1974 — The licence letters

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19741031-1 · Date: 1974-10-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

BP Pension Trust writes to Mary 'licensing' her to stay at the farm rent-free for life, and the warrant is withdrawn the same day. Mary never asked for a licence and rejects the idea that BP owns her house.

> The family's case: These one-sided letters, never accepted, became the foundation of the case that took her home.

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#letters
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### IV.9 (53). 19 November, 1970s (year unclear) — "Grievous loss"

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19741119-1 · Date: 1974-11-19 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

William Rees writes to the Western Mail that demolishing Great House Farm would erase the site of St Dochdwy's Celtic monastery, tracing its descent from Tewkesbury Abbey to the Crown, to Herbert and to Bute. The cutting is dated '19/11/7?'; the year is unclear.

- Newspaper: Western Mail, 'Grievous loss' (letter) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n04
- Wiki page: The Restoration Campaign — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/restoration-campaign/#open-day-1974

### IV.10 (54). 23 May 1975 — BP Properties

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19750523-1 · Date: 1975-05-23 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

BP Pension Trust transfers its interest to BP Properties Ltd.

> The family's case: Mary maintains that no transfer between BP companies can defeat the ownership she pleaded in 1974.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.11 (55). 1978 – 79 — The Roman villa (a separate site)

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19780101-1 · Date: 1978-01-01 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Archaeological record

GGAT excavates the Llandough Roman villa, south of the church. It is a separate site, not Great House Farm; the Neath Guardian reports the dig in April 1980.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Newspaper: Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n05

### IV.12 (56). 22 May 1980 — "The most rapacious ground landlord"

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19800522-1 · Date: 1980-05-22 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Parliament

Ted Rowlands MP tells the Commons that Western Ground Rents, 'the most rapacious ground landlord' in South Wales, has been bought by the BP pension fund. The landlord that sued Frederick in 1955 is now inside the BP group.

- Newspaper: Hansard, 22 May 1980 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n16

### IV.13 (57). 1 October 1982 — GGAT asks for a dig

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19821001-1 · Date: 1982-10-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

GGAT tells the planners that occupation may continue north of the church, and asks for 'thorough investigative work prior to the development'.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### IV.14 (58). 19 – 30 November 1982 — First registration

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19821119-1 · Date: 1982-11-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

BP Pension Trust transfers to BP Properties Ltd, and on 30 November Linklaters & Paines apply to register the land for the first time, as title WA231076. Mary is alive and living in the farmhouse throughout.

> The family's case: The family contend that nobody asked Mary, the woman living in the house, what she claimed.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1982–83 Registration & Opportunity to Object — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1982-83-registration-opportunity-to-object/

### IV.15 (59). 23 February 1983 — The farmhouse title

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19830223-1 · Date: 1983-02-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

BP's solicitors apply to register the farmhouse and garden as a separate title, WA240304, certifying they know of no question or doubt affecting the title. Mary is living in the farmhouse.

> The family's case: The family's case is that this registration took in the house parcel without disclosing Mary's claim to own it.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### IV.16 (60). 13 March 1983 — Fire at the warehouse (a separate site)

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19830313-1 · Date: 1983-03-13 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Newspaper

A fire at GGAT's Swansea warehouse destroys the finds from the Llandough Roman villa — the separate site south of the church.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 18 March 1983 — burnt relics — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n06

### IV.17 (61). 26 March 1983 — Mary dies

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19830326-1 · Date: 1983-03-26 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Mary Williams dies in the farmhouse where she was born, weeks after the registration was applied for. Her son Billy inherits her claim.

> The family's case: Whether Mary was ever told of the registration is being pursued with HM Land Registry.

- Wiki page: Mary Williams — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#death
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/#william

### IV.18 (62). 8 – 12 April 1983 — Letters after her death

Act IV: Mary's Stand · Scene id: ghf-19830408-1 · Date: 1983-04-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

Two weeks after Mary's death, Linklaters and the Land Registry exchange letters on the farmhouse file, including form D23; more letters follow on 12 May. What the Registry asked about the family's occupation, and what it was told, is in those letters. The family are ordering them.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.1 (63). 13 January 1984 — A new edition of the register

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19840113-1 · Date: 1984-01-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

An application on form A3 is made on the main title and a new edition of the register issued — four months before BP sues.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.2 (64). 22 May 1984 — BP's writ

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19840522-1 · Date: 1984-05-22 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

BP Properties issues its writ for possession, relying on the 1974 licence letters. The same year, the family say, the library copy of the Bute–Thomas deed is reported missing from Cardiff Library.

> The family's case: The licence Mary rejected became the whole of BP's case. A public copy of the deed that could answer it went missing the same year.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — the writ — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#writ
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — library copy missing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#library-1984

### V.3 (65). 10 July 1986 — Judgment for BP

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19860710-1 · Date: 1986-07-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

Mr Justice Hollis finds for BP: the 1974 letters gave Mary a licence, so her possession was not adverse. He suspends the possession order for six months.

> The family's case: In the family's account, ownership of the house parcel was never tried: the documents behind it were never examined, and the defence ran on adverse possession — a defence that began with the fields in 1955 and was stretched to cover her house.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — High Court — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#high-court
- Analysis: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/court-judicial-issues/bp-v-buckler-scope-decided-undecided/

### V.4 (66). 1986 – 87 — A file goes missing

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19860711-1 · Date: 1986-07-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

During the trial and appeal, the Royal Commission's correspondence between C.N. Johns and Mrs Buckler goes missing. It may have recorded Mary's own account of her title, given to an independent public body.

- Analysis: Legal Review — the loss pattern — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#loss-pattern

### V.5 (67). 2 February 1987 — Two titles become one

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19870202-1 · Date: 1987-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

With the appeal still pending, an application is made to amalgamate BP's two titles — the main title and the separate farmhouse title — into one.

> The family's case: The family ask why the separate record of the house parcel was being folded away in the middle of the appeal. They are pursuing it with HM Land Registry.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — amalgamation — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1987-hmlr-amalgamation-during-appeal/

### V.6 (68). 31 July 1987 — The Court of Appeal

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19870731-1 · Date: 1987-07-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

Dillon LJ, Mustill LJ and Sir Edward Eveleigh dismiss the appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. They hold that the 1962 action stopped time running, and that BP's 1974 letters made Mary's possession permissive whether she accepted them or not. The title documents she spoke of were not produced.

> The family's case: The family contend the court decided possession of the whole farm without the documents on the house parcel before it — the 1877 agreement, the 1938 conveyance, the 1939 tenancy plan — and without the 1974 press report of Mary claiming ownership or the evidence that she rejected the licence.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Analysis: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — what it omits — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#omits

### V.7 (69). 3 March 1988 — The last appeal

Act V: The Courts · Scene id: ghf-19880303-1 · Date: 1988-03-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The House of Lords refuses leave to appeal. The family are given 28 days to find somewhere else to live.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — House of Lords — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#house-of-lords

### VI.1 (70). 29 April 1988, morning — The bailiffs come

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19880429-1 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Five bailiffs and about fifteen police arrive. Billy blocks the narrow drive with a tractor, locks the doors and bars the windows.

- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on', c. 30 April 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 29 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-01) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.2 (71). 29 April 1988 — The chainsaw

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19880429-2 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The bailiffs smash the gate lock and break at the doors with poleaxes. When an axe comes through a door with his children behind it, Billy starts a chainsaw and pushes it through, and the bailiffs fall back. After a four-hour stand-off they withdraw. Branwen leaves with the children, aged two, three and four. The next day Billy will not leave the farm even for medical attention, in case they come back.

> The family's case: BP told the press Mary had been allowed to stay rent-free because of ill health. Billy told them the family owned the farm.

- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-02) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.3 (72). 3 May 1988 — To Strasbourg

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19880503-1 · Date: 1988-05-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

Billy applies to the European Commission of Human Rights.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr

### VI.4 (73). 12 May 1988 — The MP writes

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19880512-1 · Date: 1988-05-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Cardiff MP Alun Michael asks the Lord Chancellor to look at the case of the farmer who fought off bailiffs with a chainsaw. Billy warns that someone will be killed.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-03) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.5 (74). 29 July 1988 — Cadw comes to look

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19880729-1 · Date: 1988-07-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Photograph

Cadw inspects and photographs the farmhouse and barn while considering them for listing. These two photographs are all that survive of its visit: no file, no notes, no record of who decided. In 2026 Cadw gives three different explanations of the code it marked them with.

- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/#cadw-1988
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the barn, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/#cadw-1988
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/

### VI.6 (75). 29 – 30 November 1988 — Forced entry

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881130-1 · Date: 1988-11-30 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

BP obtains possession and the bailiffs force their way in. Within hours, the family say, demolition begins: half the roof is already off an outbuilding. Billy is taken to Llandough Hospital. Eight other people living at the farm are made homeless with the family.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo front page — 'Angry scenes as farmer evicted' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n14
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 November 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-04) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'Billy's unhappy family' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n09

### VI.7 (76). 1 December 1988 — Everything in the road

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881201-1 · Date: 1988-12-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy lies injured in Llandough Hospital. Branwen and the three children have nowhere to go. Mary's lifetime of possessions — photographs, heirlooms, legal papers — is left in the house or scattered in the road. Billy later says he has only the clothes he stood up in.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 13 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-11) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.8 (77). 2 December 1988 — An injunction

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881202-1 · Date: 1988-12-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A High Court judge orders that the farmhouse and its contents must not be touched. Mr Justice Anthony Evans lets Branwen go in to collect belongings if BP's solicitors agree. BP says it plans to demolish and build new homes on the 10-acre site.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'History fight to save farm' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 2 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-05) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.9 (78). 3 December 1988 — From hospital bed to the dock

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881209-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Police take Billy from his hospital bed to be charged with assaulting two bailiffs, criminal damage, and wanton or furious driving. A charge is not a conviction.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-06) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n15

### VI.10 (79). 3 – 5 December 1988 — 48 hours to decide

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881203-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Over one weekend, with no access to the inside, Cadw assesses the house for emergency 'spot-listing'. In public it says it is considering listing; in July it had already coded the house just below the bar.

- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — Cadw considering spot-listing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08

### VI.11 (80). Monday 5 December 1988 — The final hearing

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881205-1 · Date: 1988-12-05 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Judge Norman Francis refuses to keep the injunction in place until the European Commission can hear the family. Their solicitor, Colin Jongman, says there is nothing more they can do. The same day Cadw says the house is not of sufficient architectural merit to list.

- Newspaper: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — 'Farmer fails in final eviction hearing' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n10

### VI.12 (81). 6 December 1988, 4am — Bulldozed before breakfast

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881206-1 · Date: 1988-12-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Just after 4am a twenty-strong team with bulldozers moves in. By breakfast no building is left standing. Branwen and the three children watch their home flattened. The house the Royal Commission never finished recording is gone.

> The family's case: The house was destroyed the morning after the listing refusal, before its fabric could be recorded or the European Commission could hear the family.

- Newspaper: 'Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n11
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-07) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 21 December 1988 (reader's letter on "Bulldozed Before Breakfast") (search extract GHF-E090-N15-12) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VI.13 (82). 7 – 9 December 1988 — Anger in the village, and bail

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881208-1 · Date: 1988-12-07 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A Vale of Glamorgan councillor, himself a BP pensioner, calls the demolition 'disgusting'. On 8 December villagers meet their councillors in anger, and a bid is launched to stop BP profiting from it. The family recall the council's planning chief saying the cleared site looked like a battleground. On 9 December magistrates bail Billy on condition he stays away from the site.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 7 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-08) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 9 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-09) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 10 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-10) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Wiki page: 1988: Possession and Demolition — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/demolition-1988/

### VI.14 (83). December 1988 — Sifting the rubble

Act VI: The Siege · Scene id: ghf-19881212-1 · Date: 1988-12-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

R.F. Suggett of the Royal Commission examines the rubble. He finds a fireplace jamb and an ogee-stopped beam with torus, a form uncommon in Glamorgan, and records the loss of a carved stone capital that stood by the front door, probably from the old church.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VII.1 (84). January 1989 — A charge dropped

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890115-1 · Date: 1989-01-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy's bail conditions are changed, and the prosecution drops, as out of time, a summons for threatening behaviour on 29 April 1988. The November charges remain, and he is ordered not to go within half a mile of the site.

- Newspaper: 'Charge against evicted farmer dropped', January 1989 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n12
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 January 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-13) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.2 (85). 20 March 1989 — Clearing the site

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890320-1 · Date: 1989-03-20 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

At 7.30am lorries move onto the site to clear what is left. The work takes several days.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 20 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-14) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.3 (86). 23 March 1989 — "I will fight on"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890323-1 · Date: 1989-03-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy pleads guilty to the remaining charges and is freed. He vows to fight on over the loss of his home and, he says, more than 70 acres of land.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 23 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-15) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 24 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-16) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.4 (87). 1989 — From farm to a bus

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890325-1 · Date: 1989-03-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The family live with Billy's sister in Penarth. Billy plans to turn an old bus into a home, and says about £30,000 of his possessions were taken from the site after the demolition.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 1989 — 'From farm to a bus' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n13

### VII.5 (88). 14 April 1989 — Strasbourg says no

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890414-1 · Date: 1989-04-14 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The European Commission accepts that the possession order interfered with Billy's home, but finds it lawful and justified, and declares Buckler v United Kingdom inadmissible.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr
- Court record: Buckler v United Kingdom, Commission decision (PDF) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/wp-1790112811838.pdf

### VII.6 (89). 10 October 1989 — Oakview sold

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19891010-1 · Date: 1989-10-10 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Land Registry record

BP sells Oakview, title WA513690. How this land relates to the two parcels is unclear.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings

### VII.7 (90). October – November 1989 — BP applies to build

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19891107-1 · Date: 1989-11-07 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

BP lodges outline application 89/01396/OUT for housing (received 8 November). GGAT advises that it should not be decided without an archaeological assessment, prices the work at £2,000, and discloses talks with BP's agents — then BP commissions GGAT to do it. The same report calls the farmhouse a "county treasure".

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.8 (91). 8 February 1990 — Missing comments

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900208-1 · Date: 1990-02-08 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

GGAT sends further comments on the application (Appendix B). They are missing from the planning file.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.9 (92). 13 March 1990 — "Unfortunately demolished"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900313-1 · Date: 1990-03-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Outline permission is granted with 18 conditions. The officer's report notes that the Local Plan said the farm buildings should be kept, but 'they were unfortunately demolished a little while ago'. No building preservation notice had ever been served.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.10 (93). August 1990 — Eight trenches

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900801-1 · Date: 1990-08-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

GGAT digs eight machine trenches for BP. Early-medieval burials are found. The eastern area 'could not be investigated', yet is marked as low potential.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.11 (94). 15 October 1990 — Condition 17 signed off

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19901015-1 · Date: 1990-10-15 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

The council records the archaeological evaluation condition as met, on the strength of GGAT's eight trenches.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.12 (95). 21 August 1991 — The official record

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19910821-1 · Date: 1991-08-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

The regional Historic Environment Record writes up Great House Farm. It records that the house and farm buildings 'were suddenly and completely demolished by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy'.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VII.13 (96). 14 May 1992 — Twenty houses

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920514-1 · Date: 1992-05-14 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Ideal Homes Wales applies for approval of 20 detached houses on the farm (92/00671/RES) — more than a year before BP transfers the land to it.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.14 (97). 15 May 1992 — Billy dies

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920515-1 · Date: 1992-05-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Billy Buckler dies of a heart attack in Llandough Hospital. After a funeral at Bethesda Chapel, Dinas Powys, he is buried at Michaelston-le-Pit. He was born in the farmhouse and defended it to the end.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/#william

### VII.15 (98). 27 July 1992 — A warning, half missing

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920727-1 · Date: 1992-07-27 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Planning file

GGAT warns the council that the 1990 assessment showed significant deposits — medieval, possibly earlier, and human bone — and urges mitigation. Page 2 of the letter is missing from the file.

- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.16 (99). 3 September 1992 — Approved anyway

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920903-1 · Date: 1992-09-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Thirty-eight days after GGAT's warning, the 20 houses are approved with no new archaeological condition. GGAT then records no action on the site for 466 days.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.17 (100). 3 December 1993 — Groundworks begin

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19931203-1 · Date: 1993-12-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

BP transfers the site to Ideal Homes, and groundworks start before the archaeological condition has been met.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VII.18 (101). 13 December 1993 — "A difference of opinion"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19931213-1 · Date: 1993-12-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

With work already under way, GGAT urges a breach-of-condition notice, saying the archaeological condition (recorded as condition 18) has not been met. The developer relies on counsel's opinion that the condition is discharged; the council accepts it, later telling the MP it was 'a difference of opinion'.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.19 (102). March – July 1994 — A thousand graves

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19940504-1 · Date: 1994-03-21 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

Under a Home Office licence and an agreement for 'preservation by record', the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavates an early-medieval cemetery on the farm — many burials just below the topsoil, in the zone the 1990 evaluation called low potential. Published totals reach 1,026 burials, then the largest early-medieval burial population recovered in Wales. Between 21 April and at least 3 May the licence has lapsed while work continues; on 28 April GGAT's officer orders 'no further work', under an authority still unidentified. Removing remains without a licence was an offence under the Burial Act 1857.

> The family's case: The site went under 20 houses, and the evidence with it.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.20 (103). 28 July 1994 — Who owns the dead

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19940728-1 · Date: 1994-07-28 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Museum record

Ideal Homes Wales, as landowner, gives the human remains and finds from 'Great House Farm, Llandough' to the National Museum (accession 95.56H). Ownership of finds follows ownership of the land.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.21 (104). 10 November 1994 — The woodland

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19941110-1 · Date: 1994-11-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

The woodland, title WA735527, passes to the Forest of Cardiff. The wiki places it in Parcel A.

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings

### VII.22 (105). 28 June 1995 – 1996 — The last dealing

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19950628-1 · Date: 1995-06-28 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

Rights are granted to South Wales Electricity, and there is correspondence with Persimmon — the last dealing on the registration file.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings

### VII.23 (106). 2005 — The cemetery in print

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20050101-1 · Date: 2005-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

The excavation is published in Medieval Archaeology: 1,026 burials, 814 of them articulated. It tells the story of the cemetery, not of the family whose home stood beside it.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Publication: Holbrook and Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VII.24 (107). 22 December 2005 — The woodland divided

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20051222-1 · Date: 2005-12-22 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

Part of the woodland title is divided off.

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/

### VII.25 (108). 20 March 2019 — Twenty-eight years late

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20190320-1 · Date: 2019-03-20 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Heritage record

GGAT's 1990 assessment is finally added to the national record, about 28 years after it was written.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VIII.1 (109). November 2025 — Back to the records

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20251117-1 · Date: 2025-11-17 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Official correspondence

Mary's grandchildren begin a records campaign. The Royal Commission says it cannot advise on a legal case but holds archives on the site; Llandough Community Council says it cannot help; the Vale of Glamorgan passes the request to its information team.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.2 (110). 23 – 29 January 2026 — Bounced

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260123-1 · Date: 2026-01-23 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Official correspondence

The family's request to Cadw bounces: both its published addresses return 'address not found', the first of at least eight failures this year. On 29 January the family apply to HM Land Registry to record the interest left out at first registration.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.3 (111). 13 February 2026 — Retrieving the files

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260213-1 · Date: 2026-02-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

HM Land Registry sends a holding reply: it is retrieving the historic paper files.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026
- Official correspondence: HMLR holding letter, 13 February 2026 (PDF) — https://github.com/unclehowell/datro/blob/wayback/wayback/pdf/foi/2026-02-13_hmlr_wa231076_holding-letter.pdf

### VIII.4 (112). 23 March 2026 — "No evidence of a mistake"

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260323-1 · Date: 2026-03-23 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Land Registry sets out the registration history of Tŷ Mawr Farm and says there is 'no evidence of a mistake in the register'. It treats the farm as one holding and does not explain how the house parcel entered BP's title.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.5 (113). 19 April – 25 May 2026 — Complaint refused, twice

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260419-1 · Date: 2026-04-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The stage-one complaint of fraud and maladministration is refused: the Registry will not look behind the 1987 judgment. On 25 May the stage-two decision says the title is 'registered correctly'.

> The family's case: Both decisions rest on a judgment about possession, not on any deed to the farmhouse.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.6 (114). 21 May 2026 — Cadw's two photographs

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260521-1 · Date: 2026-05-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Cadw releases its two photographs of 29 July 1988, coded 'YYY' — 'marginally below the bar', it says. It has no other record and says the paper file is 'quite likely' destroyed. In July its review says 'most likely' destroyed, though there is no record of destruction.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/#cadw-1988

### VIII.7 (115). 2 – 3 June 2026 — Asking to see the originals

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260602-1 · Date: 2026-06-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family ask to inspect the original Land Registry files and ask that nothing be destroyed while the matter is open. For months there is no real answer, and several Registry addresses bounce.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.8 (116). 30 July 2026 — The missing root

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260730-1 · Date: 2026-07-30 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

Six months after the first request, the Registry releases a schedule of the 43 documents on the first-registration files. The 31 December 1969 conveyance — recited as BP's root of title — is not among them, nor is the 1971 abstract.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### VIII.9 (117). 25 August 2026 — "Not held"

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260825-1 · Date: 2026-08-25 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Official correspondence

Museum Wales refuses the family's request as 'not held', while saying in the same letter that it has found records of other discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm — which it withholds as 'not in scope'.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.10 (118). 8 September 2026 — A lead to 1877

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260908-1 · Date: 2026-09-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Glamorgan Archives hold no deeds for the 1877 Daniel Thomas sale, but point to Bute X.6(12), the Bute trustees' 1877 book of payments and receipts, now at Cardiff Library. A capital payment from Daniel Thomas in that book would prove the sale.

- Official correspondence: The 1877 Agreement — Glamorgan Archives reply — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#glamorgan-2026-4097b

### VIII.11 (119). 17 – 21 September 2026 — Complaints to Cadw and the MP

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260917-1 · Date: 2026-09-17 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family serve a formal complaint on Cadw over its 1988 listing decision and its lost file; Cadw's own address blocks it, so it is re-served on the Chief Inspector on 20 September. On 18 and 19 September they write to their MP, Stephen Doughty, with a view to a referral to the Parliamentary Ombudsman. On 20 September they ask Heneb for its records on the site. On 21 September a Land Registry agent tells them the title was 'closed in 2005' — contradicting the Registry's own history.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Wiki page: The Restoration Campaign — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/restoration-campaign/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.12 (120). 22 September 2026 — The wiki goes live

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260922-1 · Date: 2026-09-22 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Wiki

The family launch the Great House Farm Wiki, a public archive where every document is shown first, labelled by type, then explained. Nothing is kept secret.

- Wiki page: Great House Farm Wiki — Main Page — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
- Wiki page: Evidence Library — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/

### VIII.13 (121). 23 September 2026 — The Lords papers

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260923-1 · Date: 2026-09-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The National Archives identifies the House of Lords papers in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536), only added to its catalogue in May 2026. Earlier searches had found nothing.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.14 (122). 25 – 27 September 2026 — An offer on the woodland

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260925-1 · Date: 2026-09-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Forest of Cardiff, which holds the woodland title, offers the family a route to ownership. On 27 September the family decline the terms. No price is recorded for the charity's 1994 acquisition.

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.15 (123). 27 – 29 September 2026 — Heneb and the Reviewer

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260927-1 · Date: 2026-09-27 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family complain to Heneb about GGAT's role from 1982 to 1995, and take the Land Registry to the Independent Complaints Reviewer. On 28 September a preservation notice goes to eleven public bodies. Heneb appoints an investigator; the Reviewer opens case ICR/090/26.

- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.16 (124). 29 September 2026 — The armour on record

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20260929-1 · Date: 2026-09-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Cadw's complaint investigation begins. The same day the Royal Commission answers four requests together: its archive holds the 1974 newspaper report and an older note of the soldier in armour under the dining-room floor — so the story was on record long before the demolition.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/

### VIII.17 (125). 3 October 2026 — The cuttings

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20261003-1 · Date: 2026-10-03 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Wiki

Fifteen newspaper cuttings from the family archive are transcribed onto the wiki, from the 1891 court report to the coverage of 1989.

- Wiki page: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/
- Wiki page: Press Articles Index — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VIII.18 (126). 5 October 2026 — The museum releases its file

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20261005-1 · Date: 2026-10-05 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Museum record

After three requests and two refusals, Museum Wales releases the Church Farm file: the 1931 letter and the records of the medieval spur and spearhead found beside the church in 1858.

- Official correspondence: Museum Wales reply (GHF-E106-R33) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/ghf-e106-r33-amgueddfa-cymru-reply-further-collections-search-following-8-september-2026-foi/

### VIII.19 (127). 6 October 2026 — The legal review

Act VIII: The Reckoning · Scene id: ghf-20261006-1 · Date: 2026-10-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

The family publish a review of the whole record from three angles: fraud, land and human rights. Its central finding: no record yet surfaced shows how the house parcel ever entered BP's title.

- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### E.1 (128). Today — What is proven, what is missing

Epilogue: Where Things Stand · Scene id: ghf-99990101-1 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

The family's case is that the courts decided possession and never tried the house parcel on its documents — the 1877 agreement, the 1928 change, the 1938 conveyance, the 1939 tenancy plan. Those papers, BP's 1969 root of title, Cadw's file and GGAT's missing pages are still being sought. HM Land Registry, Cadw, Heneb/GGAT and the Vale of Glamorgan Council are under complaint or review, and the Independent Complaints Reviewer's deadline falls about 25 November 2026.

- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/
- Wiki page: Missing Records Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/missing-records-register/

### E.2 (129). Today — What the family ask for

Epilogue: Where Things Stand · Scene id: ghf-99990102-1 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

A ruling that they own the house parcel. The woodland and the green back, or reparations where that can't be done. Reparations for the houses built on family land. The return of the estate's artefacts. A true heritage record. Every body involved is being given the chance to put things right before the family go back to court.

> The family's case: The family's case is that fraud and deliberate concealment kept the title documents from the courts — so the judgment can be challenged under Takhar v Gracefield, with limitation postponed under section 32 of the Limitation Act 1980.
